Cekiske Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kaunas County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Jews likely first settled in Čekiškės in the late 18th century. In 1887, a fire left 160 Jewish families homeless, sparing only three houses; the population reached 432 (65 percent) by 1897. In 1915, the retreating Russian army expelled the town's Jews, preceded by a brutal pogrom. The Jewish People's Bank, established in 1920, was one of the first in Lithuania. About 60 Jewish families remained at the time of the 1940 Soviet occupation; all were murdered following the 1941 German invasion.
